P1.evidence: An application existed and the rep did use it, but 35 minutes in and as a correction of a factual detail ('From what I understood also from your application, you're currently doing like 2K steps') rather than as an opening read-back to make the prospect feel seen. The frame carried two of four parts plus a disqualification promise: 'go through where you're at at the moment, where you want to go. See if we can help you get there. If we can... If not, still point you in the right direction.' What's in the way and what you need were not named. Agreement was sought and given — 'Okay?' / 'Okay.' The open question ran verbatim: 'So tell me, what can we potentially help you with, George?'

P2.evidence: The three checks the rep ran, he ran well. Injuries and limitations were asked directly ('do you have some stiffnesses in your body, any aches, pains, anything that comes up for you?'), the training week was established properly, and nutrition got a genuinely thorough pass. Everything else was skipped. Age, height and weight were never asked in a 63-minute call — age is known only because the prospect said 'I'm already going to be 44 soon'. Occupation was never asked; it came from the application. Health conditions were never asked, and this is the consequential one: the prospect volunteered 'I have what it's called, holesteric, it's like the diagnosis, holesteric or metabolic syndrome' and a detailed kidney-stone and suspected-prostate-cancer history entirely unprompted, which under the volunteered-information rule is a miss, and the rep's only response was 'Oh yeah, yeah, yeah.' Sleep was never asked despite the prospect describing a 1-2am bedtime and an 8:30 wake. Energy was never asked despite the prospect naming 'energy level up' as one of his three opening goals. Results from current training were reached only obliquely via the 1-to-10 mirror question.

P3.evidence: The best-run Phase 3 in this batch. The 1-to-10 mirror question opened aesthetics cleanly. The bridge was asked properly and with a comparison frame: 'so many people when they're turning 44 around that age, they're okay with... not the best shape that they can be, why is it important for you, George, to get to that next level?' — which produced the Bugatti metaphor, the richest material in the call. The rep then pushed a second time ('why do you think that's important for you? Like, so many parents out there, they're okay with sort of just being an okay role model') and got the harmony answer. The future-self question ran ('take me through that version of George in a year from now'), the who-else-does-it-impact question ran twice and reached both the five children and colleagues, and the reflect-back was explicit and confirmed: 'it sounds like the reason that you want to do this, first of all, for your own energy... but also because you want to be that good example for your kids and actually teach them just life overall. Is that true?' Only the physical-thing-you-cannot-do question was skipped.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were properly excavated — five years of intermittent gym membership, swimming, YouTube-programmed sessions, and BJJ, boxing and karate when younger — and the rep clarified a genuine ambiguity rather than assuming ('just to make sure I understand it correctly, you didn't get a trainer yourself or just saw other people getting a trainer, but they didn't really get results'). What happened was drawn out well: 'it was easy for me to have gaps for half a year or more... but now it's harder, much harder.' The root-cause question ran and, when the prospect did not understand it, the rep offered options rather than abandoning it — 'do you need someone who's going to be pushing you... do you need guidance? Do you need form checks?' — and let him name the gap himself: 'I just need, like, guidance if I'm doing it correctly, correct technique... and game plan.' P4c scores partial because why-it-didn't-stick was inferred rather than asked, and P4f a miss because the information-isn't-the-problem line never ran.

P5.evidence: The first Richard Claessen call in this batch where the consequence frame appears at all, but it appears as statements rather than questions. 'It sounds like you're not willing to settle for a life where you're not going to have that, where everything stays the exact same as it currently is' is P5b delivered as a leading assertion, and the prospect answered it twice — 'What again?' then 'Ah, no, I don't want to stay the same' — with no 'why not' follow-up to make him build the case himself. The line-in-the-sand question came in a softened form and much earlier than the script places it: 'Do you feel like now it's right time for you to also commit to that aspect of your growth?' The two-year cost-of-inaction question was never asked, and the prospect had handed over exactly the material for it — an ageing body that no longer bounces back and a cancer scare at 41 — which was left entirely unused.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran before any presentation, at 00:28:00, and in full form: 'if we have all of that in place, do you then feel like you're going to be able to get to that version of you where you are more healthy, more happy, and we have more energy?' P6b ran but only after the three pillars and phrased about goals rather than about going all in: 'do you feel like if we have that in place, that there is going to be no reason for you not to get to the goals that you want?' — answered 'No. There is no reason.' The strongest single moment in the call is P6c: the prospect hedged with 'It feels this is what I'm going to try. At least, yeah. Why not?' and the rep caught it and pushed rather than banking it — 'do you feel like it comes down to trying or do you feel like it comes to doing it, sticking to the plan?' — which produced a firmer yes: 'when I usually say try, it means I'm going to stick to the plan. And usually when I start, I always finish.' That is the commitment check working as designed.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — price stated at 00:51:20, next steps laid out ('We go over the investment. If that all works, then we'll book the meeting with Trevor') — and no payment was collected. Two independent blockers: the prospect needed roughly a week to calculate what he could commit to, and there is no working payment rail for a Russian resident without a credit card. The rep did not attempt to secure a first instalment or a deposit against the follow-up. Onboarding, agreement and welcome-email steps were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation was attempted in the right place and correctly worded — 'outside of the investment, if that wouldn't be the case, would you then also be like, Richard, I just want to get started with this, but it's just the investment part that we need to figure out' — but the rep accepted a single 'Okay' as the answer and moved on without confirming nothing else was live. The upfront-then-plan move ran ('most guys, they always put it on a credit card just to be done with it, right? But I understand also that sometimes it isn't possible'). Of the six financial-picture moves only one ran: month-end surplus, which returned the most important answer in the call — 'sometimes it's nothing, because I have a lot of stuff to do... not only my family, there is also my sister's family.' Cash on hand, credit cards, available credit and used-versus-available were all skipped; crypto was raised but as a payment rail, not as an asset to liquidate. Credit to the rep for one thing the script does not require: he proactively disclosed that six payments cost $1,200 more than three and steered the prospect to the cheaper structure.

'I have to think about this' and 'I have to calculate anyway... I don't want to say now, yeah, okay, let's do it' are think-about-it triggers in substance. No OA move ran. The rep instead validated the deferral and reframed it as logistics — 'it's not like you won't, it's figuring it out' — then asked only for a date. None of 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', or the identity question were used. Partially defensible: the prospect's constraint is genuinely arithmetic and he explicitly refused to give a word he could not keep. But the play was available and untouched.

Script gap: no play, and no company process, for a prospect who cannot pay by card. The prospect is resident in Moscow, has no credit card, and pays for things by sending roubles to friends holding European cards who then transfer onward. The rep had nothing to offer — he asked 'Do you have crypto?', got no, said 'I'm just thinking of how we could do it', and ultimately left the mechanism to the prospect and his friends ('we just need to figure it out with your friends'). This is an operational and compliance gap rather than a rep failure, and it should be escalated: a payment route was improvised live with no policy behind it.

Second script gap: a prospect who explicitly does not want the accountability pillar. Asked what needed cracking, he answered 'I don't really need, like, really pushing and all this stuff, because I can push myself. I just need, like, guidance if I'm doing it correctly, correct technique... and game plan.' Accountability is a third of what is being sold and he rejected its core mechanic in advance. The rep adapted on the fly and softened it ('of course, he isn't going to be pushing you around'), which is sensible improvisation, but there is no scripted path for repositioning the offer for a self-driven buyer who wants programming and form correction only.

notes: Discovery through commitment was the strongest run in this batch — Phase 3 in particular, and the catch on 'I'm going to try' is exactly what P6c is for. Two things to fix. First, Phase 2 was three checks out of nine: age, occupation, health conditions, sleep and energy were all skipped, and a metabolic syndrome diagnosis plus a kidney-stone history arrived unprompted and were acknowledged with 'Oh yeah, yeah, yeah' and never revisited — that is a screening failure, not a pacing choice. Second, the consequence frame existed only as leading statements; this prospect handed over a cancer scare and an ageing body that no longer recovers, and neither was used.
